cleanIntro:
This guide follows CZ's CZ 75 instruction manual, which does not name the CZ 75 Legend, so check your variant against it. CZ prints one CZ 75 book for a table of versions that differ in how the pistol is made safe, and the Legend is not in that table. Every step below is quoted from that book and stated as generally as the book states it; a procedure the book gives only for particular versions is not applied here.

The strip is the CZ 75's own: hammer to the half-cock notch, the two vertical lines on frame and slide brought into line, and the slide stop tapped out from the right. The book stops the owner at the field strip and the magazine; the firing pin is a gunsmith's job.

steps.title: Know what you are holding
steps.action: This guide follows CZ's CZ 75 instruction manual, which does not name the CZ 75 Legend, so check your variant against it. Every step below is quoted from that book and stated as generally as the book states it; where the book gives a procedure for particular versions in its versions table, it is not applied here.
steps.prose: CZ's versions table lists the 75 B, B SA, BD, POLICE, DAO, COMPACT, D COMPACT, SEMICOMPACT, P-01, SP-01, SP-01 PHANTOM, SP-01 TACTICAL and MODEL 75, and sets each against its trigger operation and how it is made safe: a manual safety on some, a decocking lever on others. The Legend is not in it. Look at your own pistol before you start. Where this guide meets a control, it follows the book's own conditional wording and nothing more.
steps.quote: Among the specific features of all versions, apart from the caliber, size, weight, magazine capacity, trigger mechanism operation, surface finish, grip plate type and other specific modifications; are the methods of securing the pistol’s safety - see the following table:
steps.cite: CZ 75 — NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / INSTRUCTION MANUAL / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Pistol Description and Terminology, p.18

steps.title: Muzzle in a safe direction, magazine out
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction and keep it there. Depress the magazine catch with your thumb or middle finger. The magazine rises only a little out of the grip, so draw it clear with your other hand. Put it where you can see it.
steps.quote: Hold the pistol in your right/left hand and depress the magazine catch with the thumb/middle finger. The magazine will slightly protrude from its housing about 5 to 10 mm and then it can be removed with the other hand.
steps.cite: CZ 75 — NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / INSTRUCTION MANUAL / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operating Instructions, Removal of the Magazine, p.20
steps.warn: ALWAYS MAKE SURE THE PISTOL IS POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION!

steps.title: A manual safety, if fitted, goes to Safety-Off
steps.action: If your pistol has a manual safety, move it to the Safety-Off position, because the slide cannot be worked with it on. If it has none, go straight on. Keep your finger off the trigger.
steps.quote: 2. If the pistol is equipped with a manual safety shift it to the „Safety-Off“ position in order that the slide can be manipulated.
steps.cite: CZ 75 — NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / INSTRUCTION MANUAL / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions, Stripping for Cleaning, step 2, p.23

steps.title: Slide back, chamber seen empty
steps.action: Draw the slide fully back and watch for a cartridge leaving the ejection port. Then look into the chamber and confirm it is empty. Do not go on until you have seen an empty chamber.
steps.quote: Draw back the slide and verify the last cartridge has been extracted from the chamber and ejected
steps.cite: CZ 75 — NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / INSTRUCTION MANUAL / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Operating Instructions, Unloading the Pistol, p.21
steps.warn: MAKE SURE THAT THERE IS NO CARTRIDGE IN THE CHAMBER!

steps.title: Hammer to the half-cock notch
steps.action: Draw the hammer back slightly and let it go forward until it stops on the half-cock (safety) notch. Leave it there, neither fully cocked nor fully down, for the rest of the strip.
steps.quote: In this state the handling which follows will be easier.
steps.cite: CZ 75 — NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / INSTRUCTION MANUAL / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions, Stripping for Cleaning, step 4, p.23

steps.title: Line up the two vertical marks
steps.action: Put your left thumb through the trigger guard and grip the top of the front of the slide firmly with your other fingers. Push the slide back slightly until the vertical line on the rear of the slide sits in line with the one on the frame. Hold it there.
steps.quote: 5. Put your left thumb through the trigger guard and with the other fingers grasp the top of the front part of the slide firmly (Fig. 8). Push the slide slightly back until the two vertical lines on the rear part of the frame and slide are in line with each other.
steps.cite: CZ 75 — NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / INSTRUCTION MANUAL / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions, Stripping for Cleaning, step 5, p.23

steps.title: Slide stop tapped out from the right
steps.action: Keeping the lines aligned, push or tap the slide stop from the right-hand side of the pistol; the base of the magazine will do it. Then pull the slide stop out from the left. If it will not move, the lines have drifted apart, so realign them rather than hitting harder.
steps.quote: 6. KEEPING THE LINES ALIGNED push (tap) the slide stop from the right hand side of the weapon, i.e. using the magazine base (Fig. 9). Remove the slide stop from the left.
steps.cite: CZ 75 — NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / INSTRUCTION MANUAL / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions, Stripping for Cleaning, step 6, p.23

steps.title: Slide and barrel forward off the frame
steps.action: Pull the slide, with the barrel still in it, forward off the frame. Keep hold of it as it clears, because the recoil spring is still inside under load.
steps.quote: 7. Pull the slide and the barrel forward off the frame.
steps.cite: CZ 75 — NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / INSTRUCTION MANUAL / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions, Stripping for Cleaning, step 7, p.23

steps.title: Recoil spring and guide out, then the barrel
steps.action: Turn the slide over. Take out the recoil spring and its guide, keeping control of the spring as it comes, and then lift the barrel out of the slide.
steps.quote: 8. Remove the recoil spring and guide and finally the barrel.
steps.cite: CZ 75 — NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / INSTRUCTION MANUAL / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions, Stripping for Cleaning, step 8, p.23

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel, recoil spring and guide, and the slide stop are apart. That is as far as CZ takes the pistol for routine maintenance. After a great number of rounds, CZ adds the magazine and the firing pin; the magazine is in the deep clean, and the firing pin goes to a gunsmith.
steps.quote: No further disassembly is needed for routine maintenance. When a great number of cartridges has been fired, it is advisable to also disassemble the firing pin and magazine.
steps.cite: CZ 75 — NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / INSTRUCTION MANUAL / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions, Stripping for Cleaning, p.23

deepSteps.title: Magazine base lock pushed, base slid forward
deepSteps.action: Push in the base lock where it shows through the hole in the magazine base; if your magazine is built differently, move its base lock to the disassembly position instead. Then slide the base about 5 mm toward the front of the magazine. The spring is still held at this point.
deepSteps.quote: To remove the magazine base, push on the base lock which sticks out through a hole in the base (in case the construction is different move the magazine base lock into disassembly position) and slide the base about 5 mm towards the front of the magazine.
deepSteps.cite: CZ 75 — NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / INSTRUCTION MANUAL / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions, Magazine Disassembly, p.23

deepSteps.title: Thumb over the base, base off its rails
deepSteps.action: Cover the base with your thumb so the magazine spring cannot escape, and take the base off its guiding rails with your other hand. Let the spring up slowly under your thumb, with the magazine pointed away from your face.
deepSteps.quote: Cover the base with your thumb to prevent losing the magazine spring and with the other hand take off the base from its guiding rails. Be careful during the disassembly as the spring could fly out, or even cause an injury.
deepSteps.cite: CZ 75 — NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / INSTRUCTION MANUAL / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions, Magazine Disassembly, p.23

deepSteps.title: The firing pin is a gunsmith’s job
deepSteps.action: Do not take the firing pin out yourself. CZ hands its disassembly and cleaning to a competent gunsmith.
deepSteps.quote: Firing pin disassembly procedure and cleaning should be entrusted to a competent gunsmith.
deepSteps.cite: CZ 75 — NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / INSTRUCTION MANUAL / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions, Firing Pin Disassembly, p.23

deepSteps.title: No further disassembly
deepSteps.action: That is the end of what the book lets an owner take apart. Any adjustment or repair beyond it goes to a competent gunsmith.
deepSteps.quote: No further disassembly of your pistol is recommended. Should your pistol require adjustment or repair be sure the task is entrusted to a competent gunsmith!
deepSteps.cite: CZ 75 — NÁVOD NA POUŽITÍ / INSTRUCTION MANUAL / BEDIENUNGSANLEITUNG / MANUAL DE INSTRUCCIONES / MODE D'EMPLOI — UNKNOWN — not printed in the document — Maintenance Instructions, CAUTION, p.24

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Lightly fouled: a clean patch on the rod through bore and chamber, changing patches until the last one comes out clean
Very dirty: brush in gun cleaning solution, let it act about 10 minutes, then scrub the bore out thoroughly
Rod and brush go in from the chamber end, never the muzzle, and the brush goes all the way through before you reverse it
Dry the bore and chamber with a clean patch and check that all powder residue and fouling are gone; repeat if needed

cleaning.name: SLIDE, FRAME & BARREL OUTSIDE
tasks: Clean the other parts, including the outside of the barrel, with a dry cloth, an old toothbrush, a brass bristle brush or a wooden scraper
Preserving oil or paraffin oil can be used for this cleaning
Never use the barrel bore cleaning agent on these parts; it stays in the joints and causes corrosion later
Check that no cloth particles or brush bristles are left lodged anywhere in the pistol

cleaning.name: OIL & PRESERVE
tasks: With bore, chamber and all accessible parts clean and dry, wipe them with a cloth soaked in gun oil or spray the oil on
Wipe the barrel bore dry before shooting
In very low temperatures, take the oil off all accessible parts or use a lubricant made for those conditions
Thick preserving grease is for long-term storage in a demanding climate only, and must be removed from every part before the pistol is used

reassembly: The book prints no reassembly sequence; put the pistol back together in the reverse order of the strip.
Barrel into the slide, then the recoil spring and guide.
Slide onto the frame from the front, then push it back until the two vertical lines on frame and slide are in line again.
Slide stop in from the left while the lines are aligned, pressed fully home.
If you took the magazine apart, reverse its disassembly: spring back in, then the base slid back onto its guiding rails until the base lock holds it.
fncheck: With the magazine out and the chamber confirmed empty, work the slide by hand and check it runs fully forward with the slide stop seated. Insert an empty magazine and draw the slide back: it should stay open, as the book says it does after the last cartridge. If your pistol has a manual safety, it should go on only with the hammer cocked and should then block the trigger and the slide. If it has a decocking lever, pressing the lever should lower the hammer to the safety notch without the trigger being touched. If anything does not work this way, take the pistol to a competent gunsmith before you load it.
